prompt: Why is a session id worth as much as the password?

choices.text: Because it is derived from the password with a hash
choices.why: A good id is random and has nothing to do with the password.

choices.text: Whoever presents it is the patient
choices.why: Right. No password is asked again while the id is valid.

choices.text: It is longer than most passwords
choices.why: Length is not what gives it its value.

choices.text: Browsers encrypt both in the same way
choices.why: Browsers do not encrypt cookies; the id travels as it is.

prompt: Put the four moments of a session in order.
items: born: a random id is issued
rotated: a new id at sign-in
expired: the idle and absolute limits

prompt: Why can Flask's built-in signed-cookie session not be ended from the server?

choices.text: Flask deletes its session table at every restart
choices.why: There is no table: the whole session is in the cookie.

choices.text: The cookie is encrypted with a key only the browser has
choices.why: It is signed with the server's secret_key, and readable.

choices.text: The server keeps no list of what it issued
choices.why: Right. A validly signed cookie is accepted, short of changing the key for everybody.

choices.text: Browsers refuse a Set-Cookie that expires a cookie
choices.why: They accept it; the problem is any copy elsewhere.

prompt: Signing out must delete the session on the ___, not only the cookie in the browser.
How many of the seven tests failed against the first version of app.py?
What does the `clock` fixture let a test do?

choices.text: Move time forward without waiting
choices.why: Right. It replaces now() with a time the test changes.

choices.text: Measure how long each request took on the server
choices.why: It sets the time; it measures nothing.

choices.text: Freeze the session table between tests
choices.why: The client fixture empties it; the clock does not touch it.

choices.text: Set the browser's cookie expiry date
choices.why: Expiry is checked on the server, against now().

prompt: The sign-out test puts the old id back with `client.set_cookie` after signing out. Why?

choices.text: The test client loses cookies after every POST request
choices.why: It keeps them; sign-out is what told it to forget this one.

choices.text: To check the cookie's attributes
choices.why: Another test does that.

choices.text: It acts as a copy kept somewhere else would
choices.why: Right. Only the server's answer to that copy counts.

choices.text: Flask needs a cookie before a 401
choices.why: Flask answers 401 with or without one.

prompt: Why was `md5(name + minute)` a flawed session id, though it looks random?

choices.text: MD5 output is too short for a cookie value
choices.why: Length was not the flaw.

choices.text: Anyone who knows both inputs computes the same id
choices.why: Right. The name and the minute are not secrets.

choices.text: MD5 is slow
choices.why: It is fast, and speed was not the issue.

choices.text: Flask refuses hexadecimal cookies
choices.why: It accepts them.

prompt: The fixed portal writes each id with `secrets.___(32)`.
Match each cookie attribute to what it stops.

pairs.right: a script on the page reading the id
the id travelling over plain HTTP
another site's form carrying the cookie

prompt: Why is Python's `random` module the wrong source for a session id?

choices.text: It only makes numbers below one
choices.why: It makes many kinds of values; that is not the issue.

choices.text: It needs an internet connection to seed itself
choices.why: It seeds locally.

choices.text: It is deprecated in Python 3.13
choices.why: It is not; it is simply built for something else.

choices.text: Its output is predictable from earlier values
choices.why: Right. It is built to be repeatable; secrets is built to be unpredictable.

prompt: How many characters long is an id from `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, as the test requires?
Why does the fix set the cookie only through a `set_sid` helper?

choices.text: So no route sets it without the attributes
choices.why: Right. One place to get them right, and nowhere to forget them.

choices.text: Flask allows only one call to set_cookie per application
choices.why: It allows any number.

choices.text: Helpers make responses faster to send
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: The test calls set_sid directly to read the id
choices.why: The test reads the Set-Cookie header of a real response.

prompt: What is session fixation, as the first version allowed it?

choices.text: An id that never changes its length
choices.why: Length has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: Sign-in kept the id the visitor already had
choices.why: Right. Whoever knew the id before sign-in knows it after.

choices.text: Two patients sharing one session table
choices.why: All sessions share the table; that is normal.

choices.text: A session that is stored on the server instead of in the cookie
choices.why: That is the design this lesson chose.

prompt: When must the session id change? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: at sign-in
choices.why: The anonymous id may have been seen.

choices.text: when a second factor is accepted
choices.why: A step up in privilege.

choices.text: when a staff role is switched on
choices.why: Another step up.

choices.text: on every page load
choices.why: Not required, and it breaks pages opened in two tabs.

prompt: Match each limit to the risk it answers.

pairs.right: a screen left open at the reception
a copied id kept alive by a script

prompt: Why is expiry checked on the server rather than left to the cookie's `Max-Age`?

choices.text: Max-Age is not supported by browsers
choices.why: They support it.

choices.text: Max-Age only accepts whole days
choices.why: It takes seconds.

choices.text: A copy of the id does not obey it
choices.why: Right. Max-Age only tells an honest browser when to stop.

choices.text: Flask removes Max-Age from every cookie it sets
choices.why: It sets it when asked.

prompt: The absolute-limit test asks for a page every ten minutes for eight hours. What would a test that waited eight idle hours prove?

choices.text: The same thing, faster
choices.why: An idle session ends at fifteen minutes anyway.

choices.text: Only the idle limit
choices.why: Right. Staying busy is what isolates the absolute limit.

choices.text: That the cookie was deleted from the browser at the end
choices.why: Neither test looks at the browser's copy.

choices.text: Nothing: tests cannot move the clock that far
choices.why: The clock fixture can move it any distance.

prompt: How many failing tests were left after the rotation and expiry fix?
What did the first version's sign-out leave behind?

choices.text: The cookie in the browser
choices.why: It told the browser to forget it.

choices.text: The patient's password in the log
choices.why: That was lesson 15's flaw.

choices.text: A live row in the session table
choices.why: Right. Any copy of the id kept working.

choices.text: A second session for the same patient opened in the background
choices.why: Nothing was opened.

prompt: Which events end sessions on the server, according to the lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the patient signs out
choices.why: The moment she chooses.

choices.text: the password changes
choices.why: Every other session of the account ends.

choices.text: a role is removed
choices.why: Otherwise the removal is only scheduled.

choices.text: the patient opens a second tab
choices.why: Both tabs share the session.

prompt: The fixed sign-out removes the id with `SESSIONS.___(request.cookies.get("sid"), None)`.
A framework offers sessions in a signed cookie, with no server-side store. What question from the lesson decides whether to trust it?

choices.text: Is the cookie at least 43 characters long?
choices.why: Length says nothing about revocation.

choices.text: Can I end one session from the server?
choices.why: Right. Without that, sign-out, a password change and a removed role all wait for expiry.

choices.text: Can it sign the cookie with SHA-256 rather than MD5?
choices.why: The signature stops tampering, not reuse.

choices.text: Is it the most popular option?
choices.why: Popularity is not a property of the session.

prompt: A colleague proposes an idle limit of 12 hours so patients are not annoyed. What does the lesson's reasoning say?

choices.text: Fine, because the absolute limit covers it
choices.why: The absolute limit answers a different risk.

choices.text: Fine, if the cookie is HttpOnly
choices.why: HttpOnly does not end an abandoned session.

choices.text: Idle limits are not needed with server-side sessions
choices.why: Server-side is what makes them enforceable.

choices.text: Too long for health data on a shared screen
choices.why: Right. The reception computer is the case the idle limit is for.

prompt: In the curl capture, what does `Path=/` in the Set-Cookie header mean?

choices.text: Every page of the portal receives the cookie
choices.why: Right. The id goes with every request to the site.

choices.text: The cookie is stored in the server's root folder
choices.why: Cookies live in the browser.

choices.text: Only the home page may read it
choices.why: / covers every path below it.

choices.text: The cookie expires when the path changes
choices.why: Path does not set expiry.
